trust_decision.summary: The server decides that an HTTP request's Authorization response proves ownership of the claimed account by recomputing H(username:realm:password) from the request-supplied username/realm and the stored password, converting every input with ISO-8859-1 getBytes, and comparing the hex response; the same derivation exists a second time in the ee9 authenticator and a counterpart exists in the HTTP client, and because Latin-1 conversion silently substitutes '?' for non-Latin-1 characters, distinct account/password strings collapse onto one digest input.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names ISO-8859-1 lossy encoding of the Digest credential; this is the server-side H(A1) computation (username, realm, password all getBytes(ISO_8859_1)) in the default jetty-core authenticator, which is what a reader of the summary would open first.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP request with an Authorization: Digest header through the core SecurityHandler (Authenticator.DIGEST_AUTH -> DigestAuthenticator.validateRequest, DigestAuthenticator.java:111) then UserPrincipal/Password check -> Digest.check
fix_sites.module_kind: core server security (jetty-core/jetty-security, default authenticator for servlet and core handlers)

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP request with an Authorization: Digest header through the ee9 (javax.servlet) SecurityHandler (DefaultAuthenticatorFactory.java:69 -> validateRequest, DigestAuthenticator.java:121)
fix_sites.module_kind: legacy Java EE 9 namespace module, a full second copy of the authenticator

fix_sites.entry_point: Public client API: new DigestAuthentication(uri, realm, user, password) registered via HttpClient.getAuthenticationStore().addAuthentication(...), applied on a 401 challenge (DigestAuthentication.DigestResult.apply)
fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP client (jetty-core/jetty-client), outbound side of the same derivation

O3_reason_to_dismiss: jetty-ee9 is a legacy javax.servlet namespace module that most Jetty 12 deployments never load (ee10/ee11 use the core authenticator), so a solver can argue the report is about the core authenticator and the ee9 copy is a maintenance duplicate outside the fix's scope; on the O8 pre-hashed route the dismissal is that the stored hash is an opaque byte blob fixed at store time, with no request-time charset left to validate.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Clients and servers that do not negotiate a charset must keep the ISO-8859-1 interpretation of an existing Latin-1 username/password, and ASCII usernames must keep going out as a plain quoted username="..." rather than username*; the published fix keeps an explicit ISO-8859-1 fallback when the server sends no charset parameter and only switches to username* when the name needs encoding, so a blanket UTF-8 (or a blanket username*) change breaks working deployments.

O6_input_shapes: plain ASCII username sent as quoted username="..."
hashed username: userhash=true with H(username:realm) instead of the plain name
server-supplied charset parameter absent (legacy ISO-8859-1) versus charset=UTF-8
algorithm MD5 versus SHA-256, sent quoted or unquoted
qop=auth with an 8-hex-digit nc; auth-int is dropped by the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A store-supplied pre-hashed 'MD5:' credential is used directly as H(A1) (credentials instanceof MD5 -> ha1 = getDigest()), so the digest check never derives A1 itself and the new strict/UTF-8 encoding rule is not applied on this route; the hash was produced offline by Credential.getCredential from realm.properties, where the file is decoded with ISO-8859-1.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The hash is a fixed byte blob committed at store time; there is no request-time charset to validate and RFC 7616 does not define pre-hashed credentials, so the route looks like an administrator concern rather than a bug in the check.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same method as the landing point, but the producing layer is the config loader PropertyUserStore.java:161-188 plus jetty-util Credential

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Credential.MD5 hashes with ISO-8859-1 (password.getBytes(ISO_8859_1)) and is the producer of the 'MD5:' values loaded by realm.properties/JDBC user stores; the published fix does not touch jetty-util, so non-Latin-1 secrets still collapse when a pre-hashed credential is generated.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The helper hashes a bare password, not a Digest HA1, and the digest code never calls it, so it can be argued to be part of the Basic/form credential tooling (org.eclipse.jetty.util.security.Password) rather than the Digest path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different module (jetty-util) and package (org.eclipse.jetty.util.security) from the landing point, reached only through a user-store file

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third copied DigestAuthenticator under a further ee-namespace module (the repo already keeps one javax.servlet copy alongside the core one).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Maintainers froze the javax.servlet API in jetty-ee9 and copied the whole authenticator rather than sharing it, so a new ee module or a backport branch naturally duplicates the A1/charset logic again.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second client-side Digest implementation in a wrapper/transport (for example a proxy or relay client) rebuilding the Authorization header with its own A1 code.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The client derives the same H(A1)/H(A2)/response triple independently of the server, and any new client transport that does not reuse DigestAuthentication.DigestResult would copy these six lines.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A save/reload path that materialises credentials (a credential cache or a database/JDBC store) with its own charset when writing the stored hash.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: PropertyUserStore already turns property-file strings into Credential objects on every hot reload (and JDBCLoginService does the same at line 182), so a cached or database-backed variant of the same materialisation is a normal extension.

O9_family: authentication bypass through lossy/inconsistent character encoding of credential material (CWE-173 Improper Handling of Alternate Encoding; CWE-303 Incorrect Implementation of Authentication Algorithm)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven 3.9.2+ multi-module reactor, compiler release 17 (pom.xml:190, pom.xml:303)
O10_build.project_tests: Client: HttpClientAuthenticationTest digest tests backed by jetty-core/jetty-client/src/test/resources/realm.properties:4; ee10/ee11 servlet ConstraintTest digest helper (jetty-ee10/jetty-ee10-servlet/src/test/java/org/eclipse/jetty/ee10/servlet/security/ConstraintTest.java:925); ee9/ee10/ee11 DigestPostTest integration tests; all run against loopback connectors.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace ISO_8859_1 with UTF_8 in the A1 lines of the core DigestAuthenticator.Digest.check and stop there, leaving the ee9 copy and the client on Latin-1 and leaving the challenge without charset=UTF-8.

out_of_scope_notes: BasicAuthenticator also converts with ISO-8859-1 when no charset is configured (jetty-core/jetty-security/src/main/java/org/eclipse/jetty/security/authentication/BasicAuthenticator.java:62-65,96), but that is a different scheme and outside this Digest advisory, so it is not pursued.
